source.title: Understanding Psychological Reactance: New Developments and Findings

confidence_rationale: Anchors the V4-SOCIAL scope boundary and supplies the verdict's cleanest dissociation. Psychological reactance is 'an unpleasant motivational arousal that emerges when people experience a threat to or loss of their free behaviors,' driving restoration of the threatened freedom; it carries anger/hostility, and crucially has 'energizing and behavior-directing properties, distinguishing reactance from learned helplessness by maintaining the individual's sense of capacity to alter their situation.' That single sentence is the controllability-axis dissociation the verdict rests on: blocked-agency-with-capacity-retained (reactance/assert) is the OPPOSITE pole to suffering/helplessness (withdraw). Human social-psychology review, explicitly V4 (needs an other-agent/source of restriction), so transfer_risk is high and confidence is held at 0.62.
failure_signatures: Reactance is explicitly NOT learned helplessness: it preserves the sense of capacity to alter the situation and energizes freedom-restoration. A REE model that routes autonomy-threat / blocked-agency into the suffering accumulator (capacity-collapse, withdraw) inverts the phenomenon.

Reactance requires a threatened FREEDOM and (typically) an agent/source imposing the restriction; the four restoration strategies (direct, by-implication, aggression-at-source, subjective reappraisal) are SOCIAL/other-agent consumers -- importing them into a single-agent V3 substrate that has no model of a coercing other would be premature (V4-scope).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Reactance is an aversive motivational arousal triggered by threat to or loss of a free behavior; it intermingles negative affect (anger, hostility) with cognition, motivates restoration of the threatened freedom (directly, by implication, by aggression toward the source, or by subjective reappraisal), and has energizing/behavior-directing properties that distinguish it from learned helplessness because the person retains a sense of capacity to change the situation.
mapping.ree_translation: Defines the V4-SOCIAL boundary of the candidate stream (anti-coercion / anti-domination / autonomy-threat needs a model of an OTHER agent imposing the restriction) AND supplies the controllability-axis split the V3 proxy reuses: capacity-RETAINED + goal-retained -> assert/restore (reactance pole), vs capacity-COLLAPSED -> withdraw (suffering pole, SD-019b/Q-036). It is the clearest evidence that REE's existing withdraw-only response (suffering -> mode-switch) is missing its complementary assert pole.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human social-cognitive theory about freedom, autonomy, and an imposing source; REE-V3 is single-agent with no representation of an other-agent coercer, so the reactance CONSTRUCT proper is V4-deferred. Only its abstract dissociation (energised-assert-with-retained-capacity vs collapsed-helplessness) transfers to V3, and even that is an analogy, not a measured mechanism. High transfer risk.
mapping.source_context: Review of psychological reactance theory (Brehm lineage) and recent experimental/physiological findings in human social psychology.

confidence_components.notes: Solid review of a well-established theory but secondary and human-social. mapping_fidelity moderate: the reactance-vs-helplessness dissociation maps tightly onto the verdict's controllability axis, but the construct proper (autonomy/coercion/freedom) is V4-social. transfer_risk high: single-agent V3 has no other-agent model, so the full construct does not transfer -- only the energised-assert-pole dissociation does.
